newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's South Korean thrifts plan rescue mergers.
newsitem.headline: Japan's South Korean thrifts plan rescue mergers.

text.p: Stung by moves by ethnic North Korean financial leaders in Japan to band together, rival ethnic South Korean residents plan similiar moves to protect their economic power, provincial government sources in Osaka said on Sunday.
The planned rearrangements in both communities have been set off by problem loans they are carrying from the bursting of Japan's asset "bubble" of the 1990's.
The comparative size and financial resources of the two ethnic communities here are not known.
The sources said in the latest development, 34 small credit unions run by ethnic South Koreans planned to bail out troubled units by possibly merging into about five bigger thrifts.

"Several thrifts have been contemplating a merger scheme for a while, but their sense of crisis has picked up following last month's merger announcement by North-Korean-related credit unions," said one source close to the thrifts.
Last month, five credit unions related to ethnic North Koreans announced they will merge by next March into one unit.

Japan has several million ethnic Koreans, a legacy of its colonisation of the Korean Peninsula from the start of the 20th century until the end of World War two, when the area was split into North and South Korea.
Remittances from Japan are one of the main sources of foreign exchange for North Korea's tottering economy.

Media reports at the weekend in Osaka, an area with many ethnic Koreans, said representatives of all 34 South Korean thrifts were summoned to the South Korean embassy last Wednesday and advised to set up stronger alliances to solve their bad loans crisis.
South Korean embassy officials in Tokyo were unavailable for comment on the reports.

Although there are no details on the total amount of bad loans at the 34 South Korean thrifts, they have been heavy investors in Japan's real estate market and "pachinko" or pinball business, both areas hard-hit by the assets collapse.
Ethnic North Korean businesses were involved in the same areas.
The daily Mainichi Shimbun said in case the merger plan failed to solve problems at some especially troubled thrifts, help may be sought from banks in South Korea.
